x: Shot putter Paul Edwards ended up in the most unusual position of being beaten by a fellow Briton. His 10th placing 18.49 was topped by 1 cm by Matt Simson.
Last year Dave Smith and Lee Newman were welcome additions, while at the tail end of the 1996 season Matt Simson joined Belgrave to further strengthen an already impressive throws squad.
So too did Matt Simson, winning the 'A' shot in his first competition for Belgrave. We also welcomed Nick Dawson who gained a creditable 4th in the 'B' 200.
Mark Proctor of N&E pulled out one of those rare long putts which the rotational specialists seem to manage, so Matt Simson had to settle for second with Lee Newman winning the 'B'.

Dave Nolan's gold in the flat 400m, then Lee Hurst's silver in the steeplechase followed by wins for Matt Simson in the shot and Matt Yates in the 1500m increased our lead as Shaftesbury, Birchfield and Newham fought out the minor places.
A clean sweep in all the throws, with a remarkable 19.30 for Matt Simson in the shot, left us with a comfortable 20 points victory over Div 1 contenders Team Solent.

Last year's shot putt winner Matt Simson came up against an in-form Shaun Pickering and in spite of setting a season's best in the last round, found that he was unable to get on terms with the Haringey man.

Left: Matt Simson was clearly our best shot putter of 1998, setting a season's best of 18.44 at Gainsville, U.S.A. in April. Sadly injury wrecked much of his season - and latest news is that he has retired from the sport.
Ironically, Matt Simson was still sidelined due to the elbow operation which he had after Match 1. A blast from the past was Fred Salle, surprising everyone to win the 'A' long jump.
The results speak for themselves but the highlights were: Matt Simson's first outing since his elbow operation which limited him to the single winning effort in the shot.
